title: 6 Best Toners for Sensitive Skin: Dermatologist Recommended Picks
summary: Tired of toners that sting your skin? Explore the best facial toner for sensitive skin with soothing ingredients & expert recommendations.
body_text: Toner for Sensitive Skin Ingredients to Look for Top-rated Toners for Sensitive Skin Choosing Toner for Sensitive Skin Using Toner for Sensitive Skin FAQs You apply a toner that promises to be gentle. Within seconds, your skin starts tingling. Your cheeks look flushed, and your face feels warm and tight instead of refreshed. If this sounds familiar, you're not alone. Sensitive skin often reacts more easily when the skin barrier is weakened, and the wrong toner may leave it feeling irritated rather than soothed. A good toner for sensitive skin should do more than refresh your face. It should replenish hydration, support the skin barrier, and calm your skin without causing discomfort. Gentle, well formulated toners with soothing and hydrating ingredients can help keep sensitive skin balanced and comfortable. In this guide, we'll discuss what makes a toner suitable for sensitive skin, the ingredients worth looking for, the ingredients you may want to avoid, and our picks for the best facial toner for sensitive skin to help you build a gentle skincare routine. What Makes a Toner Good for Sensitive Skin? A good toner for sensitive skin should leave your skin feeling calm, hydrated, and comfortable, not tight, dry, or irritated. If your skin stings every time you apply a toner, it is often a sign that the formula is too harsh for your skin. Many people with sensitive skin have a compromised skin barrier, making their skin more prone to dryness, redness, and irritation. Think of your skin barrier as a brick wall. The skin cells are the bricks, while natural lipids such as ceramides act as the mortar that holds everything together. When this barrier becomes weakened, moisture escapes more easily, and irritants can penetrate the skin. A gentle toner helps replenish hydration and supports this protective barrier, leaving your skin feeling balanced and comfortable. That's why many dermatologists recommend fragrance-free, alcohol free toners that prioritise hydration and barrier support over harsh exfoliation for sensitive skin. Here are some of the key features that matter most: Hydrating Formula: A good toner should replenish moisture after cleansing and keep your skin feeling soft and comfortable, not dry or tight. Skin Barrier Support: Look for formulas that help support the skin barrier, reducing moisture loss and improving overall skin comfort. Free From Common Irritants: Choose toners without drying alcohols or added fragrance, as these ingredients may irritate sensitive skin. pH Balanced Formula: A pH balanced toner helps support your skin's natural pH and healthy skin barrier. Lightweight Texture: Whether watery, milky, or essence-like, the toner should absorb easily and leave your skin feeling refreshed without stickiness or heaviness. Ingredients to Look for in a Toner for Sensitive Skin Choosing a toner for sensitive skin can feel overwhelming, especially when ingredient lists are filled with unfamiliar names. Instead of focusing on marketing claims, look for ingredients that hydrate, soothe irritation, and support your skin barrier. Here are some ingredients commonly recommended for sensitive skin: Ceramides: These are lipids that help strengthen the skin barrier and reduce moisture loss. They keep your sensitive skin hydrated, resilient, and better protected against everyday irritants. Centella Asiatica (Cica) : It is a soothing botanical extract that helps calm visible redness and supports the skin barrier. It is especially beneficial for skin that feels irritated or reacts easily. Hyaluronic Acid and Glycerin: These humectants help attract and retain moisture in the skin. They provide lightweight hydration, leaving the skin soft, plump, and comfortable without feeling greasy. Polyhydroxy Acids (PHAs) : They provide gentle exfoliation while being less irritating than many AHAs or BHAs. They help smooth rough skin and improve texture, making them a suitable option for many people with sensitive skin. Panthenol (Vitamin B5) and Allantoin: They help soothe irritation, improve hydration, and support the skin barrier. Together, they leave sensitive skin feeling calmer, softer, and more comfortable. Ingredients to Avoid if You Have Sensitive Skin Finding the best toner for sensitive skin isn't just about what goes into the formula. It's equally important to know which ingredients to avoid. Some ingredients can leave your sensitive skin feeling dry or irritated, especially if your skin barrier is already compromised. Let’s have a look at some of the ingredients you should avoid in a toner for sensitive skin: Drying Alcohols: Ingredients like Denatured alcohol can strip away moisture, leaving sensitive skin feeling dry, tight, or irritated. Added Fragrance and Essential Oils: Fragrances and some essential oils may trigger irritation in sensitive skin. Fragrance-free formulas are often a gentler choice. High Concentrations of Exfoliating Acids: Strong AHAs and BHAs may over exfoliate sensitive skin. If needed, choose gentler PHAs instead. Harsh Astringents and Cooling Agents: Ingredients like menthol and some alcohol-based witch hazel formulas may cause dryness or stinging. Gentle, hydrating toners are a better option. 5 Best Toners for Sensitive Skin Finding the best toner for sensitive skin is not about choosing the most popular product. The right toner should suit your sensitive skin's needs, whether you want extra hydration, gentle exfoliation, or soothing care. To make your search easier, we have curated a list of some of our top picks of toners for sensitive skin that combine gentle ingredients with effective results: Products Key Ingredients Benefits Minimalist 3% Polyhydroxy Acid (PHA) Face Toner PHA, Niacinamide Gently exfoliates, hydrates, supports the skin barrier Haruharu Wonder Black Rice Hyaluronic Toner For Sensitive Skin Glycerin, Hyaluronic Acid Deep hydration, supports the skin barrier, soothes irritation Klairs Supple Preparation Facial Toner Cica Extract, Beta Glucan Hydrates, balances skin, relieves dryness SOME BY MI AHA BHA PHA 30 Days Miracle Toner AHA, BHA, PHA Gently exfoliates, controls excess oil, improves skin texture Embryolisse Eau De Beaute Rosamelis Face Toner Rose Water, Glycerin Refreshes, hydrates, soothes tired skin 1. Minimalist 3% Polyhydroxy Acid (PHA) Face Toner If your skin feels rough but reacts easily to strong exfoliating acids, this toner offers a gentler approach. It uses 3% PHA to lift away dead skin cells while helping the skin stay hydrated, making it suitable for sensitive skin that needs mild exfoliation. Let’s understand what makes it stand out: Gently Improves Skin Texture: PHA exfoliates the surface of the skin without being as harsh as many traditional exfoliating acids. Maintains Skin Hydration: Hydrating ingredients help keep the skin feeling soft and comfortable during exfoliation. Supports a Healthy Skin Barrier: The formula contains ingredients that help maintain the skin's natural balance while reducing the feeling of dryness. 2. Haruharu Wonder Black Rice Hyaluronic Toner For Sensitive Skin This toner is specifically designed to provide hydration to your sensitive skin without unnecessary heaviness. Its lightweight formula delivers moisture while helping sensitive skin feel calm and refreshed after cleansing. Here are some of its key benefits: Delivers Lasting Hydration: Hyaluronic acid helps keep the skin hydrated throughout the day. Helps Keep Skin Feeling Comfortable: Soothing ingredients leave the skin feeling more comfortable and less prone to dryness. Comfortable for Everyday Use: The fast absorbing formula layers well with the rest of your skincare routine without feeling sticky. 3. Dear Klairs Supple Preparation Facial Toner This toner focuses on restoring moisture after cleansing so your skin feels soft and balanced before the next steps in your routine. It works particularly well for skin that often feels tight after washing. Let’s have a look at its key benefits: Restores Lost Moisture: It replenishes hydration to help reduce post cleansing dryness. Helps Maintain Moisture Balance: The nourishing formula keeps the skin feeling comfortable without feeling heavy or sticky. Prepares Skin for the Next Step: Hydrated skin allows serums and moisturisers to spread more evenly. 4. SOME BY MI AHA BHA PHA 30 Days Miracle Toner If you have sensitive skin that's also prone to clogged pores or uneven texture, this toner is one of the best options that combines gentle exfoliation with soothing care. Since it contains exfoliating acids, it's best introduced gradually to allow your skin time to adjust. Let’s understand why it stands out: Removes Dead Skin Cells: A combination of exfoliating acids helps keep the skin looking smoother and clearer. Refines Skin Texture: Regular use can improve the appearance of rough or uneven skin. Helps Keep Pores Clear: The formula helps remove excess oil and impurities that can contribute to clogged pores. 5. Embryolisse Eau De Beaute Rosamelis Face Toner This refreshing toner provides lightweight hydration while leaving the skin feeling fresh and comfortable after cleansing. Its floral water based formula absorbs quickly without a heavy or sticky finish. Here are some of the reasons it stands out: Refreshes the Skin: It leaves the skin feeling fresh and revitalised after cleansing. Lightweight and Comfortable: The non-greasy formula absorbs easily without leaving a sticky residue. Softens the Skin: It helps keep the skin feeling smooth, supple, and comfortable with regular use. How to Choose the Best Toner for Sensitive Skin There isn't a single toner that's perfect for everyone with sensitive skin. Some people struggle with dryness and flaking, while others deal with excess oil, occasional breakouts, or frequent redness. That's why choosing the toner for sensitive skin starts with understanding your skin's biggest concern. To make your decision easier, we have broken down which type of toner works best for different sensitive skin concerns. For Dry and Flaky Skin: Choose a hydrating toner that relieves dryness and keeps your skin feeling soft and comfortable after cleansing. For Oily and Acne Prone Sensitive Skin: Opt for a lightweight toner with gentle exfoliating ingredients that help manage excess oil without irritating the skin. For Red and Easily Irritated Skin: Choose a fragrance-free toner with soothing ingredients and avoid harsh exfoliating formulas. Consider Your Existing Skincare Routine: Pick a toner that complements your routine, especially if you already use active ingredients like retinol or exfoliating acids. Always Patch Test: Before using a new toner on your face, patch test it on a small area of skin for 24 to 48 hours. If irritation occurs, discontinue use and switch to a gentler formula. How to Use a Toner on Sensitive Skin Using a toner correctly is just as important as choosing the right one. A gentle application helps your skin get the most benefit while reducing the risk of irritation. Here are some simple steps that you should follow when using a toner on sensitive skin: Start With a Gentle Cleanser: Cleanse your face with a gentle cleanser and lukewarm water, then pat your skin dry, leaving it slightly damp. Apply the Toner: Apply the toner with clean hands or a soft cotton pad using gentle patting motions instead of rubbing. Let It Absorb: Allow the toner to absorb for a few seconds before applying the next skincare product. Follow With a Moisturizer: Apply a moisturizer to help lock in hydration. In the morning, finish with a broad-spectrum sunscreen of SPF 30 or higher. Hydrating toners can be used once or twice daily, while exfoliating toners should be introduced gradually, starting with two or three times a week. Final Thoughts Finding the best toner for sensitive skin is all about choosing a formula that meets your skin's unique needs. A well formulated toner can hydrate, support the skin barrier, and keep your skin feeling comfortable without causing unnecessary irritation. Paying attention to the ingredient list and selecting products designed for sensitive skin can make a noticeable difference to your daily skincare routine. Whether you are looking for lightweight hydration, gentle exfoliation, or extra barrier support, the right toner can help keep your skin healthy and balanced. However, if your skin continues to sting, burn, or become irritated despite using gentle skincare products, it is best to consult a dermatologist to identify the underlying cause and receive personalised treatment recommendations.

title: ENISA's Updated Procurement Guidelines Are About to Make Medical Device Security a Contract Requirement, Not a Nice-to-Have
summary: ENISA's July 2026 procurement guidelines turn NIS2 supply-chain rules into contract requirements for medical devices, covering MDS2, UDI-DI, and IEC 62304.
body_text: ENISA, the EU Cybersecurity Agency, released updated procurement guidelines for the cybersecurity of hospitals and healthcare providers in July 2026 — a follow-up to its 2020 guidance. The timing isn't coincidental. It's the direct implementation piece of the Commission's January 2025 action plan on hospital cybersecurity, and it's designed to give hospitals a concrete, checklist-driven way to satisfy their NIS2 supply chain obligations at the exact point where those obligations are hardest to enforce: procurement. It's guidance, not law — ENISA is explicit it doesn't override national regulations. But it enables hospitals and healthcare providers to implement laws and regulations, such as NIS2 obligations for risk management and incident reporting, that extend into how they buy. This document is ENISA operationalizing that legal reality into something a procurement team can build into an RFP. ‍ For medical device manufacturers and the hospitals that buy from them, this document turns abstract NIS2 risk-management language into specific contract requirements that purchasing departments can now incorporate in their tenders.. 1. Why procurement is the pressure point ‍ The health sector absorbed 8% of all ransomware incidents tracked in ENISA's 2024 Threat Landscape report, and earlier ENISA data found only 27% of healthcare organizations have a dedicated ransomware defense program. ENISA's diagnosis is that legacy devices, thin security budgets, and sprawling multi-vendor supply chains are the structural reasons the sector keeps getting hit. NIS2 (Directive (EU) 2022/2555) already requires essential and important health entities to manage supply chain risk, but the directive itself doesn't tell hospitals how to realize these requirements in RFPs or contracts. That's the gap this guidance fills — and it does so by walking through the full procurement life cycle (plan, source, manage) with device-specific, auditable checklist items. ‍ 2. What changes for medical devices specifically ‍ Medical devices/IVDs get their own dedicated use case in the guidance (a networked radiology fleet — CT and MRI machines — being procured by a large hospital), and it's the most fleshed-out of the three scenarios. Some of the concrete asks hospitals are now expected to write into device procurement: ‍ Request the MDS2 (Medical Device Security Disclosure) form from every device supplier during procurement, and confirm bids show evidence of MDR alignment and standards like ISO 27001 or IEC 62304. Verify a UDI-DI (unique device identifier) is assigned and documented, with intended purpose and full variant/accessory descriptions. Confirm that devices are correctly classified under MDR Annex VIII (Class I/IIa/IIb/III) with justification, since that classification drives how much scrutiny the device gets. Require remote maintenance access to be VPN + MFA, session-limited, logged, and disabled by default when not in active use — no standing/permanent accounts. Require hardware sourced only from authorized manufacturers or certified distributors, with digital signatures or device certificates proving firmware integrity at first boot. Require software validated to IEC 62304, with a patch management process that includes testing on non-production samples and documented compensating controls for devices that can't be patched (a real issue for older imaging or life-support equipment). Build in supplier obligations for vulnerability disclosure and incident notification aligned to NIS2's 24-hour early-warning / 72-hour reporting clock. Plan for secure decommissioning — certified data sanitization and asset tracking so a retired device can't leak patient data or get quietly reused. ‍ None of these are new concepts to anyone who has followed MDR post-market surveillance or IEC 62443/62304 work. What's new is that ENISA is packaging them as procurement checklist items with explicit identifiers (e.g., requirements SOURCE-04.02, MANAGE-05.03) that a hospital's legal and IT teams can drop straight into tender documents and supplier scorecards. ‍ 3. Why hospitals will actually adopt this ‍ Three things push adoption beyond "here's some good advice": ‍ Legal traceability: NIS2 requires essential/important entities to demonstrate risk-based supply chain management, and management bodies can be held accountable under Article 20 for failing to oversee it. A codified checklist gives hospital boards and CISOs something they can point to during an audit or after an incident: "we followed the ENISA-endorsed procurement measures relevant to this device class." It's the default answer to an unresolved question: Most hospitals don't have in-house expertise to translate NIS2's principles-based language into device-specific contract clauses. ENISA has effectively done that translation for them, which lowers the cost of compliance to "adopt the checklist" rather than "build one from scratch." It reallocates the burden to suppliers: Because the guidance tells hospitals exactly what to demand — MDS2 forms, UDI-DI documentation, IEC 62304 validation evidence, patch SLAs, incident notification clauses — device manufacturers that can't produce this documentation on request will simply lose bids. That market pressure is likely to move faster than regulatory enforcement alone. ‍ 4. The practical takeaway for device manufacturers and hospitals ‍ If your device doesn't already ship with an MDS2 form, documented UDI-DI, IEC 62304 validation evidence, a real patch management commitment, and a defined incident-notification SLA, expect EU hospital tenders to start asking for exactly that — this document is likely to become the reference checklist procurement teams cite. The guidance also treats AI-enabled device functionality as a distinct disclosure category (model provenance, data flows, human oversight), so devices with embedded AI/ML features should expect additional documentation requests beyond the baseline MDS2-style disclosures. ‍ For hospitals, the message is similarly direct: NIS2 compliance for medical technology isn't going to be demonstrated primarily through firewalls and SOC dashboards — it's going to be demonstrated through what you required, and got, from suppliers before you signed the contract. ‍ 5. Conclusion ‍ Taken together, these guidelines mark a shift from cybersecurity-as-afterthought to cybersecurity-as-contract-term in EU hospital procurement. ENISA hasn't created new legal obligations — NIS2, MDR, and GDPR already impose them — but it now has given hospitals a practical way to act and implement. ‍ With a ready-made checklist, explicit device-class use cases, and identifiers that map straight to tender language, adoption becomes the path of choice for procurement teams that are under audit pressure, and a competitive necessity for device manufacturers who want to keep winning EU hospital contracts. Most of this maps to practices manufacturers already invest in for MDR/IVDR and SDLC hygiene; where it goes further is making signed software delivery and end-of-life planning explicit, checkable procurement criteria tied to winning the deal. ‍ Expect this document to become the de facto reference for tenders within upcoming procurement cycles, with the manufacturers who can readily produce MDS2 forms, UDI-DI documentation, and IEC 62304 evidence gaining an edge over those who can't. ‍ --- Source: ENISA, "Procurement guidelines for the cybersecurity of hospitals and healthcare providers," July 2026 https://www.enisa.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2026-07/Procurement%20guidelines%20for%20the%20cybersecurity%20of%20hospitals%20and%20healthcare%20providers.pdf ‍

title: How To Use GEDmatch - Is It Safe? | Beginner's Guide
summary: We’re introducing GEDmatch — one of the most popular tools to track down your family members and family history using raw DNA data files.
body_text: *Have you taken a DNA test already? Here’s how you can download your raw DNA data files from 23andMe , Ancestry , and MyHeritage so that you can upload them to sites like Genomelink and get more value from the same DNA test. In this tutorial article, we’re talking about what is GEDmatch , how to upload your DNA data from different DNA testing services into GEDmatch, and explaining each function and how it can maximize your DNA relative match. GEDmatch is one of the most popular tools to track down family members and learn about your family history. Using raw DNA data that you can get from a genetic DNA testing kit kit from companies like 23andMe or AncestryDNA, GEDmatch allows you to dive deep into techniques used in genetic genealogy. Although GEDmatch is an extremely powerful tool, there is quite a learning curve on how to use GED match effectively. Plus, keep in mind that GED match was recently purchased by a company that specializes in cold cases, crime scene forensics, and uses the genealogy site to solve crimes. Follow along with us to see exactly how you can start using your raw DNA data to research your family history using GEDmatch! What Is GEDmatch? GEDmatch.com is a great family finder tool for people who are interested in finding your relatives for FREE. The website offers a suite of professional-grade genealogy research tools that are not for the faint-of-heart! GEDmatch got its roots when at-home consumer genetic DNA testing services started allowing users to download their raw data. With this genetic data, GEDmatch can run a suite of statistical techniques to help you fully understand your genetic heritage. Previously a non-profit company, the company was recently purchased by Verogen, Inc., a company that focuses on forensic evidence for law enforcement. The database on the GEDmatch site was one of the first DNA databases that police used to identify criminals - namely the Golden State Killer, who had avoided authorities for 40 years! Verogen clearly valued GEDmatch’s database, which was purchased along with the company . While site policy still allows you to “opt-out” of giving police access to your data, having a database law enforcement can use is clearly now a goal of the company. Even distant relatives with DNA in the database can improve law enforcement matching and it makes genomics a useful tool for catching criminals. ‍ Is GEDmatch Safe? Though GEDmatch started as free service allowing users to search for family members using their DNA data, the company was purchased by forensic company Verogen. Though the acquisition raised some concerns about user's DNA privacy and the transfer came with some issues, the company still provides users with the option of opting-out of law enforcement searches. The company seems to be abiding by this policy, as there was only one initial issue that resulted from a breach in the system. The issue has been resolved, and no new reports of unwanted law enforcement access have been reported. However, you may want to know more about this incident to put your mind at ease. In July 2020, the GEDmatch database was breached by hackers . As a result of this incident, the privacy controls on millions of user accounts were overridden. For about 3 hours, this breach allowed law enforcement agencies to see the data of millions of users who had not given their consent. While the site was shut down quickly and the privacy settings were restored, the breach started calls for GEDmatch to be more transparent about their cooperation with law enforcement. For example, companies like 23andMe and Ancestry regularly publish reports that detail the times they were required to disclose user information for legitimate legal reasons. This seems to have been a one-time issue for GEDmatch, though caution is warranted if you do not want law enforcement officials to access your private data without a search warrant. ‍ How To Use GEDmatch How to Upload Data to GEDmatch To begin, you must register on GEDmatch.com. First, upload your DNA data from DNA testing companies like AncestryDNA . After receiving the test results of your common ancestor, these companies allow you to download your own raw DNA data and upload that elsewhere to access different information, like GEDmatch. List of companies whose raw data are compatible with GEDmatch (links to respective pages explaining how to download raw DNA data): AncestryDNA (Ancestry.com) 23andMe MyHeritage Family Tree DNA (FTDNA) LivingDNA Plus, GEDmatch now claims that “most other” company files are also compatible with their system! ‍ Once you’ve downloaded your raw data file, create a GEDmatch account and upload your raw DNA data. (We’re writing a step-by-step guide on how to do this in another blog post). Note that it will take a few hours after uploading to see your results. They don’t notify you when it’s ready — but you can check the “Kit ID”, and if it says no kit number registered yet, you need to wait a little longer. What is a kit number on GEDmatch? After you upload your raw DNA data for DNA analysis, the company will assign you a kit number. Your kit number is a unique identifier tied directly to your DNA profile on GEDmatch. The kit number will allow you to share your profile with friends, allow them to find you on GEDmatch, and you can search other kit numbers to compare with. Kit numbers have a standardized format, which also allows you to see where certain sources of data come from. This is useful if you are trying to track down relatives, as you will get the best results if you submit a DNA data from the same source because the exact same sites will be tested. This will give you the most accurate results. ‍ ‍ DNA Application: Once you have added your DNA analysis, you are ready to begin exploring! Start on the right-hand side of the page, under “DNA Applications”. This is where all of the free tools reside on GEDmatch. Simply click on each of the tools to get started. Remember: you will need your kit number for most applications. GEDmatch is commonly used by professional genetic genealogists for genealogy research. The core features include: One-To-Many DNA Comparison Result : Helps you compare your genetic profile to users in the GEDmatch database. Emails are provided so you can quickly contact them if you get a hit. This is a simple and great resource for telling if you are related to anyone in the GEDmatch database. One-to-One Autosomal DNA Comparison : This helps you narrow down the comparison with one specific relative member. Use this to confirm how much DNA data you actually share with that person before you reach out. Admixture (heritage) : This is a well-known DNA analysis for identifying your ethnic roots. Like Ancestry DNA and 23andMe, it shows the proportion of your DNA coming from a particular ethnicity/geography. It’s interesting to compare these results with that of other ancestry DNA testing kits. However, there are numerous other tools listed on the GEDmatch homepage that you can use for different purposes (as pictured below). For first-timers, we recommend starting out with the 3 tools listed above (boxed in red in the image below). ‍ However, once you get accustomed to the free tools, consider upgrading to the Tier 1 package to get some really incredible tools. ‍ You can find each tool on the menu bar above. ‍ GEDCOM Files You may have noticed that GEDmatch also allows you to upload GEDCOM files, which store information about family trees. Using a GEDCOM file from Ancestry, MyHeritage, or any other family tree software, you can compare your GEDCOM file to all files within the database, allowing you to see exactly how your family tree ties into other people’s family trees. You may even be able to see where you shared a common ancestor! Tier 1 Tools Though we won’t get into how to use the advanced GEDmatch DNA tools here, it is worth noting: they are pretty cool. Here is a short description of some of the coolest tools GEDmatch users get access to: Lazarus : Essentially, you can recreate a dead person’s genetic code using samples from their close relatives. While it won’t bring them back to life - it is very helpful for using DNA information from an autosomal DNA test to do deep genetic genealogy research. Phasing : This tool sorts out your chromosomes by using information from your mother and/or father. This allows you to see exactly which parent gave you that crooked nose! My Evil Twin : Your parents could have created many versions of you, based on which genes they passed on. This simulation essentially recombines your genetics to estimate what traits your “evil twin” would have carried. There are many other traits available in Tier 1, allowing you to explore specific segments of your DNA and many other statistical analyses! ‍ How To Understand The Results Once your results are ready, you are able to explore a number of features on GEDmatch . Here are the two main tools: How to Find My DNA Relatives? 1. One-To-Many DNA Comparison Result When you click “One-To-Many DNA Comparison Result”, you can see a list of contacts like below. How do you evaluate the results to determine who is a potential relative? Check “Overlap and Total cM” first. ‍ One-To-Many DNA Comparison Result View ‍ “Total cM” is the total length of all substantial DNA segments you share with a DNA match. “Overlap” is the total number of overlapping SNPs that you share with your match. SNPs are “ single nucleotide polymorphisms .” You can think of them simply as DNA letters important in determining your unique genetic profile. Therefore, the larger the number of centimorgans you share with another user, the more closely you are related. The table* below summarizes the total cM expected from different degrees of relations within the family. For example, if your parents’ data is on GEDmatch, they should show up as a match with over 3000 cM shared. If you do it with great-grandparents, it would be around 464-1486cM. Or 46-515cm with a 2nd cousin. However, GEDmatch also gives you the ability to change and modify this search. You can learn more about how your “match thresholds” can change your results on the ISOGG Wiki . ‍ Degree of family relation implied from “Total cM” ‍ *If you want further details, DNApainter’s comprehensive chart of cM calculator does a good job of explaining this. Note that DNA data files and their coverage of the genome differ across companies, so results may inevitably not be 100% accurate. Cited from DNA painter under CC4.0 license ‍ In conclusion, by checking “Overlap” and “Total cM”, you may find people who share a significant amount of DNA with you — people who potentially are your newfound relatives! ‍ 2. One-To-One Autosomal DNA Comparison Once you find someone who shares a good chunk of DNA data with you, you can start digging into the details of your DNA relationship with them. The image below is from the One-To-One DNA Comparison Result: it gives you a visual representation of which segments of your DNA you share with that person (chromosome browser). What you want to see is how many blue chunks do you have. Settings to generate your One-to-One DNA Comparison Results ‍ Blue matching segments have significantly common DNA data between you and your match ‍ This one-on-one matching can really help you narrow down who you are related to and how much DNA you share with that person. You can also start to track which segments of DNA you share with different people - little puzzle pieces in the story of how you came to be. ​ A Review of What Else Can We Do With GEDmatch? One-To-Many DNA Comparison Result and One-To-One DNA Comparison Result are awesome tools to start with. Besides those, here’s our recommendation for what else to try. Try out Admixture / Oracle with Population Search. This helps you learn what genetic ethnicity you have based on publicly available genealogy databases such as MDLP, Eurogenes, Dodecad, etc. Here is a summary of the recommended databases to use based on your ethnicity: MDLP — European, American Eurogenes — European, American Dodecad — Eurasians, Asians, Africans HarappaWorld — South Asian Ethiohelix — African puntDNAL — (Unknown) GedrosiaDNA — Eurasian (Indian and Asian) Heritage view on GEDmatch ‍ Are Your Parents Related? This “fun” tool allows you to see if your family is prone to inbreeding. You would be surprised - it is more common than people think, though the relationship is usually very distant. This tool essentially compares each “phase” (maternal or paternal portion) of your DNA to see if they are related to each other. X-DNA Comparison Using FamilyTreeDNA X-DNA data, you can compare your X-DNA directly to other users that have uploaded their data. One to One X-DNA Comparison is a unique feature that enables you to do the same comparison as "One-To-One DNA Comparison", specifically for your X Chromosome. The main One to One comparison tool analyzes autosomal DNA, which is your numbered chromosomes commonly used by ancestry DNA companies. Y-DNA can trace your paternal line (father's side), X-DNA does the same for your mother's side maternal line. The One to Many X-DNA comparison allows you to compare to all the users in the database at once and see if you share the same haplogroup and what percentage of the X-DNA you share. For males, X-DNA is very telling of their maternal DNA ancestry (similar to mtDNA). You can learn more about how to use this tool on this post as well! "How to Understand Gedmatch X One-to-One Results" ‍ Everything You Need to Know Before Starting with GEDmatch ‍ GEDmatch.com is one of the top family finder tools for people who are interested in locating unknown or lost relatives for FREE. The website offers a suite of professional-grade genealogy research tools that provides comprehensive solutions for genetic genealogy and family tree search. They also have tools to help estimate ethnicity and heritage and help trace shared ancestors. ‍ GEDmatch allows users to upload their raw DNA data from genetic testing companies like 23andMe or AncestryDNA to search for relatives and learn about their family history. Their website is chock full of features that can be used to analyze and understand the user's genetic data and find relatives, such as chromosome browsers, ancestry painting, and one-to-many searches. It’s a powerful tool, but has a steep learning curve that can feel confusing to some users. ‍ Before getting started, many amateur family researchers ask: “Is GEDmatch safe to use?” Previously a non-profit company, GEDmatch has since been purchased by Verogen, Inc., a company that specializes in forensic evidence for law enforcement. This acquisition raised some concerns about user privacy, however, the company still provides users with the option to opt-out of law enforcement searches. So far, that assurance has been enough to convince tens of thousands of family researchers to use GEDmatch’s services. That said, no system is perfect - in 2020 the site was briefly accessed by hackers. ‍ To use GEDmatch, users must first register on the website and then download their raw DNA data from DNA testing companies like AncestryDNA. They then upload this data to their GEDmatch account and wait a few hours for their results to be processed. GEDmatch is compatible with raw DNA data from AncestryDNA, 23andMe, MyHeritage, Family Tree DNA, and LivingDNA, to name a few. Users can then use various tools on the website to search for relatives and learn about their family history. ‍ GEDmatch also allows you to upload GEDCOM files, which store information about family trees. It can be used to create a family tree and contains information about relationships, events, and other details about a person's life. GEDCOM files can then be uploaded to GEDmatch, where they can be compared to other GEDCOM files, which allows you to see other GEDmatch users who might be your relatives! Some users find navigating the GEDmatch process and ensuing results to be…less than straightforward. Follow the steps and images in this blog, which are designed to walk you through the process. Still feeling lost? There are other less complicated online resources for exploring your genetic ancestry. Get started for free today with Genomelink, which we’ve designed to be user friendly and full of information and findings you won’t get anywhere else. ‍ Overall, GEDmatch DNA analysis is a useful tool for anyone interested in finding relatives and learning about their family history. However, users should be aware of the potential privacy issues and the possibility of law enforcement access to their data. If you’re comfortable with the risks, and with navigating the process, using and learning from GEDmatch can be a truly eye-opening experience. ‍ Conclusion Was this GED match review helpful? title: Battery Storage Is No Longer Just a Solar Add-On
summary: Battery Storage Is No Longer Just a Solar Add-On
body_text: For years, commercial energy optimization followed a familiar formula: install rooftop solar, pair it with battery storage, and finance the project through a long-term Power Purchase Agreement (PPA). When the site is suitable, it remains one of the most effective ways to reduce energy costs without upfront capital. But many facilities don't have enough roof space, favorable structural conditions, or cost-effective utility interconnection to support solar generation. Until recently, those buildings had few meaningful alternatives. Today, battery storage has become a compelling standalone solution capable of reducing demand charges, improving energy resilience, and lowering operating costs even without on-site solar. What Battery Storage Solves on Its Own The core financial problem that battery storage addresses is peak demand charges , the fee utilities levy based on a facility's highest 15-minute power draw in a given billing period. Utilities assess demand charges because they must maintain enough grid capacity to meet a customer's highest moment of electricity usage, even if that peak lasts only a few minutes each month. Demand charges can account for 30-50% of a commercial facility's total electricity bill, and they cannot be reduced through energy efficiency measures alone. A facility that cuts its overall energy consumption by 20% through lighting upgrades and HVAC optimization will see minimal reduction in demand charges if its peak demand profile remains unchanged. Battery storage with intelligent dispatch addresses this directly. A properly configured battery energy storage system (BESS) charges from the grid during low-demand periods and dispatches stored energy during high-demand windows, preventing the facility from reaching the peak setpoints that drive demand charges. Depending on the facility, this can reduce demand charge exposure by 40-60% through effective peak demand management. That financial benefit exists entirely independent of whether the facility has any solar generation at all. The battery charges from the grid, dispatches intelligently, and the utility meter records a lower peak. The demand charge savings are real and they compound every month over the life of the system. Beyond demand charge reduction, a battery storage system provides backup capability during grid outages. Even without solar generation to recharge the battery during an extended outage, a properly sized system can maintain critical loads for hours, long enough to bridge most short-duration grid events that account for the majority of commercial facility outage experiences. Beyond lowering utility costs, battery storage is increasingly viewed as a resiliency asset. Healthcare facilities, distribution centers, manufacturers, and municipalities all face growing pressure to maintain operations during grid disruptions. Even without solar generation, commercial battery storage can keep critical systems online during short-duration outages while backup generation starts or grid service is restored. The Emerging Commercial Model As battery storage has matured as a standalone product, the financing structures supporting it have evolved alongside the technology. The Power Purchase Agreement, which works well for solar-plus-storage deployments where the developer owns generation assets producing measurable kilowatt-hours, is not always the most natural fit for a pure storage deployment. An increasingly common alternative is the Energy Savings Agreement, sometimes called a Shared Savings Model. Under this structure, a third-party energy developer deploys and operates a commercial energy storage system at a commercial facility at no upfront cost to the facility. Rather than charging for energy delivered, the developer takes a share of the documented demand charge savings the system generates, typically determined by an independent auditor comparing the facility's demand charge exposure before and after deployment. The financial alignment in this model is direct. The developer captures value only when savings are real and verified. The facility pays nothing unless the system performs. And because there is no upfront capital requirement, the facility's balance sheet is not affected. This model opens the commercial energy optimization market to a significantly broader set of facilities than solar-plus-storage PPA structures alone can serve. Any commercial or industrial facility with meaningful demand charge exposure, regardless of its solar potential, is a candidate. Solar Plus Storage Remains the Ideal None of this suggests that battery storage replaces solar. For facilities where rooftop or ground-mounted solar is practical, combining generation with intelligent storage remains the most comprehensive energy infrastructure solution available. Solar offsets grid consumption during daylight hours, reducing the energy cost baseline. Storage captures and dispatches that solar generation intelligently, reducing peak demand charges. Together, they compound the financial benefit in ways that neither achieves alone. The point is not that storage is better than solar-plus-storage. It is that storage alone is no longer a consolation prize for facilities that cannot do solar. It is a legitimate, financially compelling first step for those facilities, and increasingly, a core component of a broader energy strategy that may eventually include generation as well. The market is moving in this direction. Battery costs have declined significantly over the past several years. Intelligent dispatch software has matured. At the same time, evolving grid reliability standards, increasing electrification, and growing resiliency requirements across many jurisdictions are creating conditions where battery storage deployments will continue to accelerate across commercial and industrial markets. What NextNRG Builds NextNRG designs and deploys AI-driven energy systems that integrate battery storage, on-site generation, and intelligent energy management for commercial and industrial facilities, healthcare campuses, municipal operators, and fleet-intensive organizations. We begin by evaluating how a facility consumes electricity rather than assuming every project requires the same solution, and we structure projects under both Power Purchase Agreement and Energy Savings Agreement models, selecting the financing structure that best fits each facility's specific circumstances and objectives. For facilities where solar is viable, we deliver integrated solar-plus-storage systems under long-term PPAs that eliminate upfront capital requirements and lock in long-term energy cost predictability. For facilities where solar is not viable, we deploy intelligent battery storage systems under Energy Savings Agreements that generate real, audited demand charge reduction with no upfront cost to the facility. Contact the NextNRG team at nextnrg.com to discuss which model fits your facility's energy infrastructure needs. title: How to forward a landline to a cell phone in 4 steps
summary: Don’t miss a beat while you’re on the go. We’ll teach you how to forward a landline to a cell phone or stay connected with virtual numbers.
body_text: If there’s one thing every customer can agree on, it’s that businesses should answer the phone. You can avoid long hold times and missed calls by using the call forwarding option on your landline. To forward a landline to a cell phone, lift the handset, dial *72, wait for the dial tone, enter the 10-digit cell number, then press # and wait for the confirmation tone. To turn it off, dial *73. On most US carriers (AT&T, Verizon, CenturyLink) *72 turns forwarding on and *73 turns it off. Some carriers also offer Selective Call Forwarding, which lets you forward calls only from specific numbers you choose — for example, CenturyLink’s *63 . Carrier call forwarding is usually included in your plan, but forwarded long-distance or international calls may be billed per minute. Here’s what you need to know about how to forward a landline to a cell phone and a solution that makes the process easier. How to forward a landline to a cell phone Using the unconditional call forwarding feature on your landline, you can reroute your calls to your cell phone number. Keep in mind the exact process can vary depending on your desk phone model. To forward your landline to a cell phone, follow these steps: Dial *72. Type in the 10-digit phone number that you want to forward calls to. Press pound ( # ). Wait for a confirmation tone before hanging up. Note: After the confirmation tone, some carriers like AT&T automatically call the forwarding number to confirm it’s reachable. If that line is busy or doesn’t answer, forwarding won’t activate. If you hear an error message, just repeat the steps. On other carriers, the call going to voicemail counts as answering. If you only want calls to be forwarded when you’re on another call, you can set up busy call forwarding to automatically redirect calls. To turn off call forwarding and take calls on your landline again, dial *73 and wait for the confirmation tone. Keep in mind you can still place outgoing calls from the landline while forwarding is on. Landline call forwarding codes by carrier Phone provider Turn on forward all calls Turn off forward all calls Selective/ Conditional call forwarding Verizon Dial *72 followed by the 10-digit forwarding phone number. Dial *73 . Contact support AT&T Dial *72 , enter a forwarding number, and then press # Dial *73# . Dial *90 , enter a forwarding number, then press # for busy forwarding. Dial *91# to turn off. Dial *92 , enter a forwarding number, then press # for no-answer forwarding. Dial *93# to turn off. CenturyLink Dial *72 , then dial the forwarding number. Dial *73 . For Selective Call Forwarding, dial *63 to turn on and *83 to turn off. For the full star code breakdown for mobile phones and how to forward only when busy, see conditional call forwarding codes . 5 Limitations of forwarding a landline Carrier forwarding solves the basic problem of missed calls when you’re busy, but it comes with real gaps: You can only forward to one number at a time. There’s no way to split calls across a team or route them based on who’s available. You can’t answer on the landline while forwarding is on. You may hear a brief ring as a reminder, but the call itself has already gone elsewhere. Forwarded long-distance or international calls may bill per minute , even if your base plan includes forwarding at no charge. No call recording, screening, or analytics . You don’t get a record of calls for compliance or training, and spam callers get directed to the same forwarding number. There’s no shared access either, so if more than one person needs visibility into calls, forwarding alone can’t provide it. You’re toggling codes by hand every time you leave or come back , with no way to schedule it. If the code isn’t taking effect at all, or calls are still ringing the landline instead of forwarding, see why call forwarding isn’t working for troubleshooting steps. Virtual numbers: A better alternative to call forwarding A virtual business number on your cell means no second phone in your pocket and no customer ever seeing your personal line. Your team gets work numbers that ring the right device without anyone juggling two handsets. Plus you can take calls from your computer, tablet, or smartphone via WiFi. Here’s how you can set up a virtual number in Quo: Set up a virtual number Getting started with Quo is quick and easy. Here’s how you can set up your virtual number in just a few minutes: Create a Quo account — when you sign up, you can try Quo free for seven days. Pick a phone number — choose a local US, Canadian, or toll-free number by searching for an area code or city. Download the app — after completing the sign-up process, including selecting your plan, download the iOS or Android app to start calling, texting, and customizing your phone settings. Now you have a virtual phone number you can use to work from anywhere with an internet connection. But what if you need to forward calls when you’re not working? That’s where shared numbers come in. Separate business from personal There’s nothing worse than getting business calls on your mobile device after work and feeling pressured to answer. VoIP systems let you have two phone numbers on one phone , making it easy to distinguish between incoming personal and business calls. Plus, you can keep your personal number private and exclusively use a business phone number that forwards to your cell phone for work. Share access to a phone number When someone calls a team’s shared number, it rings everyone with access so any available rep can answer. The whole team can also make calls, send texts, and view all conversations in one place, keeping everything organized. Here’s how to share a business number with teammates in Quo: Open the Quo app. Go to Inboxes. Then tap … on the Phone number you want to share. Click Add users . Enter the email address of the person you want to share the number with and choose their role (Admin or Member). Click Send invitation . Once a teammate accepts the invite, they’ll have access to the shared number. On their cell phone, the Quo mobile app lets you know if an incoming call is from a Quo number, making it easy to distinguish business calls from personal ones. Here’s how this works out for one Quo customer: “As a real estate agent, I’m fielding calls almost 24/7 but Quo has made it easy for my team to help. With one local phone number, we all receive the calls and texts which allows for the quickest and best customer service. It’s very easy to use and I love that I’m able to go back to the dashboard and look at my team’s activity. I would recommend Quo to anyone looking for a way to simplify client communication!” — Frank McKnew, President & CEO, McKnew Realty Group Text from your virtual number OpenPhone supports SMS and MMS messages , so you can send anything from text and images to videos and GIFs. It also makes texting easier with features that help you save time and respond faster: Auto-replies that let you set clear expectations when your team is busy or away. Text message templates ( snippets ) , so you can quickly reply to common questions without typing the same message over and over again. Scheduled texts that help you stay TCPA compliant by making sure you only respond to customers during business hours in their timezone. Never miss a call No solid internet connection? No worries. With Quo, you can set up call forwarding on the web, desktop, and mobile apps, ensuring you never miss an important call . Want the in-between step first? A business phone number that forwards to your cell keeps your personal number private without switching your whole setup. “The absolute best part about Quo is how easily it lets me keep my business and personal life completely separate. I don’t have to carry around a second physical work phone or deal with a confusing, clunky setup… The shared inbox features are a massive plus, allowing multiple team members to stay completely aligned, view message threads, and jump in to answer calls or texts so we never let an estimate or client follow-up slip through the cracks.” — Quo user on G2 | Read full review How to port your landline number to Quo Switching to a virtual number is quick and painless, as it should be. Under the FCC’s local number portability rules , you can transfer your existing number to a new provider as long as you’re staying in the same general area. You can port your landline phone number to Quo in a few simple steps: Find out if you can port your phone number . Tell your landline service provider you’ll be porting out. Complete our phone number porting form in the Quo app. It only takes a few minutes, but it’s helpful to have your account number, account PIN, landline number, and latest phone bill or invoice ready. Wait 5-7 business days for your porting request to be processed. If you want to send text messages to US numbers, complete the US carrier registration . Once complete, Quo will inform you of your porting date and time. After the port is complete, you’re all set to cancel service with your landline provider — but avoid canceling before your virtual number is activated to avoid service interruptions. Weighing your options beyond traditional carriers? Find the best call forwarding apps . FAQs Is it free to forward a landline to a cell phone? Activating forwarding with *72 is usually included with landline service at no extra monthly charge. But your carrier still bills the forwarded leg of the call — so forwarding to a long-distance or international number can incur per-minute charges even if the base feature is free. With a virtual number like Quo, forwarding to numbers in the US and Canada is included. What are the call forwarding codes for major landline providers? On AT&T and CenturyLink, *72 turns forwarding on and *73 turns it off. AT&T also offers busy (*90/*91#) and no-answer (*92#/*93#) forwarding. CenturyLink offers selective forwarding (*63) but doesn’t publish busy/no-answer codes. Codes vary by region and equipment — contact your provider for the most accurate information. Can I still receive calls on my landline while forwarding is on? Not with standard (*72) forwarding. Every call goes straight to your cell phone, and you can’t answer on the landline while it’s active. To keep taking calls on your landline and only forward the ones you miss, you’ll need busy or no-answer forwarding instead. How do I check if call forwarding is active on my landline? Most landline carriers don’t publish a dedicated status-check code. The *#21# check used on mobile phones is a cellular-specific code and doesn’t apply to landlines. The most reliable way to confirm forwarding is active: call your landline from another phone and see where it rings, or check your account through your carrier’s website or app. Why isn’t call forwarding working on my landline? A few common causes: the forwarding number is busy or doesn’t answer when your carrier tries to verify it (voicemail picking up usually counts as answered), the number was entered incorrectly, or the feature isn’t included in your plan. How do I turn off call forwarding on my landline? Dial *73 and wait for the confirmation tone. If you set up busy or no-answer forwarding instead of standard forwarding, you’ll need the matching deactivation code.

title: Kapton® Returns to the Moon
summary: Qnity (formerly DuPont Electronics), announced today a multiyear contract with European power module manufacturer Semikron-Danfoss who will integrate Pyralux® AP all-polyimide double-sided copper clad laminate into its eMPack® power modules to further enhance the capabilities of next-gen electric vehicles.
body_text: On November 16th, NASA successfully debuted its Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and the Orion capsule with a long-awaited launch from Kennedy Space Center, for what will be a more than month-long journey around the Moon. And as was the case for the first missions to the Moon, Kapton® polyimide films are onboard. Artemis is NASA's program to return astronauts to the Moon by 2025, eventually preparing the way for human missions to Mars. Artemis I is an uncrewed flight test, to get ready for the Artemis II crewed mission around the Moon in mid-2024. The Artemis III manned lunar landing mission planned for 2025. A key part of the Artemis program is eventually creating a Moon-orbiting space station called Gateway, that will provide essential support for long-term human return to the lunar surface and will serve as a staging point for deep space exploration. Kapton® polyimide film is used throughout Artemis and the mission’s associated payloads to reduce the electrical conductivity between cables and other components, shield the cables from radiation, and reduce Electromagnetic Interference (EMI). The PTCS (Passive Thermal Control Subsystem) also utilizes Kapton® thermofoil heaters to protect the electronics from extreme cold temperatures. Thin and lightweight, these foil heaters can be bent to handle a range of curves and irregular surfaces. Multilayer Insulation (MLI) blankets made from Kapton® are helping to help protect the spacecraft from extreme hot and cold temperatures. The Orion capsule will travel 280,000 miles from Earth and will stay in space longer than any human spacecraft has before without docking to a space station and will return home faster and hotter than any previous lunar mission. About two hours after the launch, Orion separated from the Interim Cryogenic Propulsion Stage (ICPS) and deployed ten small satellites, known as CubeSats, to study the sun, the moon and even near-Earth asteroids. As Orion continues to the Moon, it will be propelled by a service module provided by ESA (European Space Agency) that will course-correct as needed along the way. The service module supplies the spacecraft’s main propulsion system and power.
